s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative spinal infection with neurological deficits
salient_findings: Cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness
Enterobacter cloacae cultured from wound and blood
key_facts: Diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
History of radiotherapy for laryngeal cancer
Underwent thoracoscopic esophagectomy with retrosternal gastric tube reconstruction
Developed cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge on postoperative day 4
Underwent salvage reconstruction with free jejunal autograft and pectoralis major muscle flap coverage
Developed worsening low back pain and fever 15 days after reconstruction
MRI of lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5

shortlist.label: Spondylodiscitis
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings of decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4-L5, consistent with disc infection

shortlist.label: Epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of neurological deficits, fever, and elevated white blood cell count, suggesting a spinal infection

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings and clinical presentation consistent with vertebral body infection

shortlist.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
shortlist.why_kept: Enterobacter cloacae cultured from blood, suggesting a bacterial infection of the spine

shortlist.label: Discitis
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings and clinical presentation consistent with disc infection, a common cause of postoperative spinal infection

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening low back pain and fever, combined with the MRI findings of decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5, are consistent with spondylodiscitis, an infection of the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae. The presence of Enterobacter cloacae in blood cultures further supports this diagnosis, as it is a known cause of spondylodiscitis.

rejected.label: Epidural abscess
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings do not specifically indicate an abscess in the epidural space.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While osteomyelitis is a possible diagnosis, the MRI findings are more specific to spondylodiscitis, which involves the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae.

rejected.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
rejected.why: This term is sometimes used interchangeably with spondylodiscitis, but spondylodiscitis is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's symptoms and MRI findings.

rejected.label: Discitis
rejected.why: Discitis is a possible diagnosis, but spondylodiscitis is a more comprehensive diagnosis that includes infection of both the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae.
